response.answer: Kang Wang is a leading researcher in extreme cardiac MRI analysis under respiratory motion, notably for the CMRxMotion challenge. His work focuses on improving image quality and segmentation despite motion artifacts. He collaborates with many experts in the field.

results.content: # Title:Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis under Respiratory Motion: Results of the CMRxMotion Challenge. View a PDF of the paper titled Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis under Respiratory Motion: Results of the CMRxMotion Challenge, by Kang Wang and 48 other authors. The challenge comprised two tasks: 1) automated image quality assessment to classify images based on motion severity, and 2) robust myocardial segmentation in the presence of motion artifacts. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the challenge design and dataset, reports the evaluation results for the top-performing methods, and further investigates the impact of motion artifacts on five clinically relevant biomarkers. | Cite as: | arXiv:2507.19165 [eess.IV] |. |  | (or  arXiv:2507.19165v1 [eess.IV] for this version) |. results.content: The images of training set (20 volunteers) along with the annotations are released to the challenge participants, to develop an automated image quality assessment model (Task 1) and an automated segmentation model (Task 2). Therefore, we launch the extreme cardiac MRI analysis challenge under respiratory motion (CMRxMotion Challenge) 1, to establish a public benchmark dataset to assess the effects of respiratory motion on CMR imaging quality and examine the robustness [9] of automated segmentation models. CHALLENGE TASKS Based on the curated CMR dataset, we proposed two tasks: to develop an automated image quality assessment model (Task 1) and an automated segmentation model (Task 2). In this task, we expect the challenge participants to develop an image quality assessment model to evaluate respiratory motion artifacts. All images with diagnostic quality (i.e., Label 1 & 2 in Task 1) in training, validation and test set are segmented by an experienced technician (X.K.) in 3D Slicer and reviewed by two radiologists (Z.S. and C.D.).
